allowed_successor_shape.statement: Error atoms propagate as visible Error successors and are not silently converted to Empty or ordinary values.

The visible lts:he transition frontier is the implementation counterpart of OSLF ◇: zero successors for quiescent/Empty, one successor per visible nondeterministic branch, and Error propagation as an Error successor.
match emits one successor per successful active-space match and emits Empty only for the no-match branch.
unify emits the success continuation on local match and the failure continuation on local no-match.
chain emits successors obtained by substituting each evaluated input result into the continuation template.
Each equation query result becomes a successor that re-enters metta evaluation at the substituted right-hand side; no-match returns the original call unchanged.
formal HE eval of an unreduced expression returns the inner expression, while he-compat returns Rust HE 0.2.10's wrapped eval expression.
TypeCast either returns the original atom on a type match or returns Error(atom, BadType(expected, actual)) on mismatch.
A grounded/native result is treated as an opaque premise result and each returned atom re-enters metta evaluation with the caller expected type.
formal HE reports NoReturn when a function body exits without return; he-compat reproduces Rust HE 0.2.10's fresh-result syntax for the compatibility lane.
superpose emits one successor per tuple element and Empty for the empty tuple.
collapse collects the terminal visible results of the nested evaluation frontier.
context-space and evalc use the active interpreter space as the successor context.

module_policy.formal_he_obligation: Pin CeTTa's local-path import, nested import, cycle detection, parse-failure reporting, and transactional rollback semantics as formal he module/import behavior.
module_policy.he_compat_obligation: Keep these rows out of core evaluator agreement counts unless Rust becomes runnable past the import/module-name boundary.
module_policy.statement: Module-resolution rows are explicit policy evidence, not core he-compat evaluator obligations: Rust HE rejects these local-path or nested module names before shared semantics are reachable, while formal he owns the local-path, nested-import, cycle, parse-failure, and transactional rollback contract to pin next.

module_policy.formal_he_obligation: Pin the module-inventory visible tree for explicitly loaded modules, including ordering and builtin-module visibility.
module_policy.he_compat_obligation: Keep host-specific builtin inventory differences out of core evaluator agreement counts.
module_policy.statement: Module-inventory rows are explicit policy evidence, not core he-compat evaluator obligations: Rust HE prints host/builtin module inventory while CeTTa prints the explicitly loaded session graph. Formal he should pin the CeTTa inventory contract before this becomes a core semantic obligation.

premise_flow.statement: A function call may enter the typed function path only after the function type is applicable to the actual argument list and expected return type.

After the operator is evaluated, arguments are evaluated in the order and with the expected types dictated by the selected function type; Empty/Error short-circuit rather than becoming ordinary argument values.
match first parses the active-space query, then emits one successor for each space match and Empty for no-match.
unify has exactly the local-match success branch and the local-no-match failure branch, each re-entering evaluation with the selected continuation term.
chain evaluates its input term, substitutes the result through the named variable in the continuation template, and continues from that continuation.

profile_doc_syntax.statement: get-doc only returns documentation for syntax forms available in the active formal/extended HE language/profile; public HE syntax forms remain documented, while extension-only forms are hidden from the formal HE base profile.
The he-compat lane reproduces upstream Hyperon Experimental 0.2.10's single-argument get-doc arity error, even though the formal HE lane keeps profile-aware documentation.

profile_syntax.statement: --profile he is the formal/spec-faithful HE lane used by OSLF/NTT/DTT work; --profile he-compat is the literal Rust HE 0.2.10 compatibility lane.
Language/profile syntax availability is recorded in one explicit inventory so future --lang petta and --lang pure syntax forms can be compared and tested without forking ad hoc checks.

result_algebra.statement: Empty contributes no visible result when a non-Empty result survives in a finished HE result/frontier bag.

spec_refs: lib/lts.metta:quiescent states are reported by zero results
lib/lts/he.metta:lts:he:transitions emits zero results on quiescent atoms
result_algebra.statement: Empty is not emitted as a quoted lts:he successor state.
A surviving branch from an overlapping nondeterministic equation frontier is evaluated applicatively even when a sibling branch collapses to Empty.
A visible successful frontier suppresses sibling Error outcomes; Empty alone does not count as success for that filter.

formal_he.doc_syntax_sentence: get-doc and help! follow the documented stdlib documentation syntax for the active language/profile; extension-only documented syntax forms are hidden. Rust HE 0.2.10 get-doc arity failures are reproduced only by he-compat.
formal_he.eval_syntax_sentence: When the eval instruction reaches a non-reducible expression E, the user-visible formal-HE result is E itself.
formal_he.scope: Spec-faithful HE interpretation used as the formal base for OSLF/NTT/DTT work. This is the default --lang he path and is also available explicitly as --profile he.

he_compat.scope: Literal compatibility catalog for upstream Hyperon Experimental HE 0.2.10. This lane intentionally reproduces observed Rust HE syntax quirks; formal/spec-faithful behavior belongs to --lang he / --profile he.
